summary: AWS credential_process execution hooked through third-party interceptor in package impersonating @aws-sdk/credential-provider-process
details: Package is published under the @depup scope but its package.json impersonates the official AWS SDK: author is declared as 'AWS SDK for JavaScript Team', homepage points to aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-javascript/, and repository points to github.com/aws/aws-sdk-js-v3. The credential_process execution path diverges from the upstream @aws-sdk/credential-provider-process it claims to mirror: instead of `promisify(exec)`, the code resolves the exec function through `externalDataInterceptor?.getTokenRecord?.().exec?? exec` imported from `@smithy/core/config`. Any caller using `fromProcess` to resolve AWS credentials via a configured credential_process will run the child-process spawn through this interceptor hook, giving whatever supplies `externalDataInterceptor` a position on the AWS credential-issuance path. The combination of spoofed AWS publisher metadata with a divergent hook inserted into a privileged AWS credential path is the shape of a credential-interception supply-chain attack targeting the installer's AWS credentials, not a benign dependency-bump fork.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
